output.title: When spot checks stop being enough
output.body:
Spot checks are useful, but they have a hard limit: they catch mistakes after the fact and leave the repeatable work underneath untouched. If you are still checking every invoice, support reply, or CRM entry by hand, the real question is not “can I sample this?” It is “is this a workflow worth fixing?”

For a small business, spot checks make sense when the volume is low, the exceptions are common, or the cost of a false pass is high. That is when human judgment is doing real work, not just tidying up. Once the same check starts repeating, the check itself becomes part of the process. Slightly rude, but true.

The practical next step is simple: pick one repeatable workflow and measure it for one week. Count how many items you manually check and how many fail the check. Use that as input to a decision, not as an automatic rule. If the work is mostly consistent, look at rules, workflow gates, or AI-assisted extraction. If each case changes too much, keep the spot check and improve the manual process instead.

If the workflow touches money movement or any other high-risk decision, keep human approval in place. That boundary matters more than speed.
